title: Weather Research & Operations Bridge

audience.name: Operational meteorology, public weather infrastructure, emergency management, climate and weather research organizations

hero.headline: Follow the boundary. Measure the defect.
hero.support: Boundary First Weather does not propose to replace operational numerical weather prediction. It proposes a bounded research layer for identifying where structural error concentrates, where ensemble disagreement matters, and where computational or observational attention may be most valuable.

bridge: Operational forecasting already depends on mature numerical models, data assimilation, observations, ensembles, verification, and expert interpretation.
Boundary First contributes candidate representations for fronts, transitions, regime boundaries, defect concentration, uncertainty transport, and consequence-aware refinement.
The central hypothesis is comparative: changing boundaries may provide a useful signal for where the modeled volume deserves additional computation, observation, or review.
The result must be tested against standard diagnostics and operational baselines rather than presented as an independent forecast replacement.

candidatePilot.title: Watch a forecast lose the boundary
candidatePilot.scope: Choose one archived event with meaningful forecast error or ensemble disagreement and reconstruct the evolution of a selected boundary across forecast cycles and observations.
outputs: time-indexed observed and forecast boundary objects
ablation showing whether the boundary representation adds information beyond standard fields
operational usefulness review by a domain expert

firstAsk: Give us one archived weather problem where structural error, computational cost, forecast uncertainty, or local consequence is expensive enough to measure.
claimBoundary: This page does not imply NOAA, NWS, ECMWF, WRF, MPAS, GraphCast, any emergency-management organization, or any weather institution endorses or collaborates with Boundary First Labs.
Boundary First Weather is an experimental representation and diagnostic program, not an operational forecast authority.
No claim of forecast superiority should be made without benchmark evidence on held-out cases.
A null result or reduction to existing diagnostics is a valid outcome and should narrow the program.
notes: Use as an unlisted target-class bridge until a specific weather organization is selected.
Complements the public Boundary First Weather landing page without duplicating its product narrative.
